evidence.note: Rough ordered build plan emerges: db.rs/migrations/snowflake IDs first, then main.rs with all routes. Foundational DB schema correctly sequenced before feeds — a sensible ordering signal.

Build was largely monolithic: one giant main.rs with all ~40 handlers written at once, then iterative compile-error fixing. Not independently verifiable subsystems; done-check was mostly 'does it compile'.
Health endpoint verified early via curl after first successful build — a genuine done-signal for the skeleton milestone.

Remaining work repeatedly enumerated as feature lists (404 JSON, security headers, rate-limit, ETag, CSRF, audit). Reactive per-step planning rather than a written milestone plan; done-signals stayed shallow (compile + ad-hoc curl of health/404/RSS).

Risky/foundational shared-state pieces (x-request-id, rate-limit wiring, CSRF) were deferred to the very end and left as placeholders/incomplete — the opposite of sequencing hardest interfaces early, and no parity check per milestone.

reasoning: The agent broke the port into recognizable subsystems (db/migrations → routes → feeds/search/media → middleware/headers → HTML → admin/audit) in a broadly sensible order and used rough done-signals (health/404/RSS curl, successful compile), matching anchor 5. It falls short of 8 because there was no concrete per-milestone parity check against the reference, no written/referenced milestone plan (TodoWrite reminder ignored), the core was built monolithically, and the riskiest shared-state/header-contract pieces (CSRF, request-id, rate-limit) were sequenced last and left incomplete rather than de-risked early.
